comments.text:
`trace()` deletes a functions attributes; filing this under 'Documentation' since maybe this is just a behavior that needs documenting:

```
foo = function() {
  1+1
}
attr(foo, "key") = "value"

invisible(trace(foo, browser))
"key" %in% names(attributes(foo))
# [1] FALSE
```
comments.creator: michaelchirico4

comments.text:
This is true, but `untrace(foo)` returns them. Maybe the documentation should be changed from

> The trace function operates by constructing a revised version of the function  
> (or of the method, if signature is supplied), and assigning the new object back  
> where the original was found.

to specify that the trace version  only includes the body of the function.

comments.text:
(In reply to Elin Waring from comment #1)
> This is true, but `untrace(foo)` returns them.

That's right, but not too surprising -- the `trace()`'d object attaches the original as an attribute:

```
foo1 = function() {
  1+1
}
foo2 = foo1
invisible(trace(foo1, browser))

identical(attributes(foo1)$original, foo2)
# [1] TRUE
```

Which is simply "plonked" back into place on `untrace()`.

The question is whether the `trace()`'d object is _supposed_ to retain its attributes. In my case, doing so is useful because the function is an S3 object whose methods refer to the attributes. So `trace()` breaks the associated methods because the referred attributes are gone.

(NB: this is related to https://bugs.r-project.org/show_bug.cgi?id=18354, where it's now confirmed that `trace()` is supposed to be working better with S3-classed functions)
